title: Design a Cache-Safe Dashboard
prompt:
Cache expensive shared information while ensuring private user data cannot leak between users.

Submission: a small reviewable artifact, relevant tests, expected outputs, one failure/boundary case, and version/environment notes. Use synthetic data. Django/Python server code is not executed by CodeLeaf browser preview; local or human review is required.
target_skills: Choose cache keys whose scope matches the data’s visibility.
Define expiry/invalidation rules and a stale-data policy.
Test that users with different permissions never share private responses.

starter.content:
from django.core.cache import cache

def get_featured():
    value = cache.get("catalog:featured:v1")
    if value is None:
        value = build_featured_catalog()
        cache.set("catalog:featured:v1", value, timeout=60)
    return value
starter.code:

expected_output: The cached function is suitable only for data safe to share across callers.
acceptance_criteria: A public aggregate uses an explicit TTL.
Private data is scoped safely or not cached.
Tests cover invalidation and user isolation.
State whether verification was local, static, or human-reviewed.
Do not claim a build/deployment or external integration was tested unless it was actually run.
hints: Start with low-risk shared catalog summaries.
Never use a global cache key for personalized/private content.
Invalidate or refresh cached values after relevant writes.
grading_method: Required-string smoke check plus human review of technical correctness, tests, safe handling, expected result and reproducibility. This does not execute arbitrary Python/Django code.
retry_policy: Retries are allowed after reviewing feedback; the platform backend owns its uniform XP/idempotency rules.
